# opencode-cli

Minimal CLI to talk to an [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) server over HTTP + SSE.
Zero npm dependencies — pure TypeScript, runs with [Bun](https://bun.sh/).

## Why

The official opencode server exposes its HTTP API directly. This CLI gives you a
one-shot `prompt "1+1=?"` from your shell, without spinning up the TUI or
writing a custom integration. Targets opencode **1.18.x** (verified on
`1.18.35`).

## Install

```bash
bun install
bun link      # optional — exposes `opencode-cli` in PATH
# OR run directly:
bun src/cli.ts ...
```

Requires Bun ≥ 1.3.

## Usage

```text
opencode-cli health [--port X] [--host H] [--base-url URL] [--json]
opencode-cli session new   [--base-url URL] [--json]
opencode-cli session list  [--base-url URL] [--json]
opencode-cli session show <id>    [--base-url URL] [--json]
opencode-cli session messages <id> [--base-url URL] [--json]
opencode-cli prompt <text>... [--base-url URL] [--port X] [--session ID]
                              [--stream] [--json]
```

Default base URL: `http://localhost:4096`. Override with `--base-url`,
`--port` + `--host`, or the env var `OPENCODE_BASE_URL`.

### Examples

```bash
# Health
opencode-cli health
# → {"healthy":true,"version":"1.18.35"}

# Quick prompt (synchronous, v3 endpoint)
opencode-cli prompt "1+1=?"
# → 2

# Streamed output (best-effort SSE; falls back to sync if SSE unavailable)
opencode-cli prompt --stream "explain quicksort in one paragraph"

# Reuse a session
opencode-cli prompt --session ses_xxx "continue the previous answer"

# JSON output (for piping into jq)
opencode-cli session list --json | jq '.[].id'

# Talk to a remote server
opencode-cli --base-url http://box.local:4096 prompt "hello"
```

## Endpoints (opencode v3)

| Method | Path                       | Used by                              |
| ------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| GET    | `/global/health`           | `health`                             |
| POST   | `/session`                 | `session new`, prompt auto-create    |
| GET    | `/session`                 | `session list`                       |
| GET    | `/session/{id}`            | `session show`                       |
| GET    | `/session/{id}/message`    | `session messages`                   |
| POST   | `/session/{id}/message`    | `prompt` (sync)                      |
| GET    | `/session/{id}/event`      | `prompt --stream` (best-effort SSE)  |

The `prompt` command uses the **synchronous** `/session/{id}/message` endpoint by
default — returns the full assistant message with `info.finish` and `parts[]`.
When `--stream` is set, the CLI also opens the SSE stream and incrementally
writes new text to stdout; if the server's SSE endpoint is unavailable (e.g.
returns the SPA fallback HTML), the CLI gracefully degrades to the sync result.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (default, no server needed)
bun test src/

# End-to-end (requires running opencode server on http://127.0.0.1:4096)
OPENCODE_E2E=1 bun test src/
```

The e2e suite sends `Reply with the single word: pong` (sync) and
`Reply with the single word: stream-ok` (stream) and asserts a non-empty
response with `finish === "stop"` / `"session.idle"`.

## Error handling

- Non-2xx HTTP responses throw with status code + body preview
- `info.finish === "error"` or non-null `info.error` throws with the server message
- Stream timeouts are not imposed by the CLI; it waits for the opencode server response (v2 poll + SSE 自然终止：assistant+idle / session.execution.succeeded) until completion — stop a stuck request with Ctrl+C
- Exit code is `0` on success, `1` on prompt/stream failure, `2` on argument errors

## Development

```bash
bun test src/ --parallel 4     # fast feedback
OPENCODE_E2E=1 bun test src/   # with real server
bun src/cli.ts --help
```

Files:

- `src/client.ts` — HTTP client (zero deps, fetch-injectable)
- `src/sse.ts` — SSE block / buffer / stream parser
- `src/prompt.ts` — `sendPrompt(client, text, opts)` orchestration
- `src/cli.ts` — argv parser + dispatch + main entry (`bun src/cli.ts`)
- `src/*.test.ts` — TDD unit tests
- `src/e2e.test.ts` — real-server e2e (skipped unless `OPENCODE_E2E=1`)
